fixes.explanation: Fair guess, friend, because Samaria is in this passage. It's the city the Assyrians come marching against later, though. Hezekiah is king of Judah, and the text says he reigns in Jerusalem. Hold on to Samaria, because we're going back there.

That's it, friend! The text says he "…cut down the Asherah poles." That's three jobs in a row: removing, shattering, cutting. It's like someone who wipes the counter, then the floor, then the oven door too.

Moving them indoors is like sliding the burnt batch to the back of the cupboard and hoping nobody notices. That's not what the text says, friend. It says he "…cut down the Asherah poles." Down means down.
Nothing in the text says the snake was cracked, friend. The reason is right there in verse 4: "…for up to that time the Israelites had burned incense to it." That's what the writer tells us.

True! The text says, "No king of Judah was like him, either before him or after him." Before AND after, friend. That's a long line of kings, and the writer says none of them were like Hezekiah. Right before that line, the text says he trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel.

Serve! The text says Hezekiah "…rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him." That's the king of a powerful empire, and Hezekiah says no. And that same verse says the LORD was with Hezekiah.

Visit makes it sound like a social call, friend. The text is stronger than that: he "…rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him." This was a rebellion, not a scheduling conflict. The word is serve.
Meet is a little too small a word, friend. The text says he "…rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him." The word is serve.

The Moabites don't show up in these verses, friend. The text says, "He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders…" Plenty of nations in the Bible, and it's easy to mix them up. Keep your eyes on the Philistines this time.
The text counts longer than months, friend. It says, "And at the end of three years, the Assyrians captured it." Three years of siege on Samaria. I think this part of the story is a heavy one.

Not Egypt, friend. The text says, "The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes." So the exile is to Assyria and those places.

False is right, friend. The text says, "The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes." Egypt isn't named here.

Walls aren't mentioned anywhere in this passage, friend. The reason is stated in verse 12: "…they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant…" That's what the writer says. I'd rather stick to what the text gives.
